column4:
Over current 
Current is 1.5 times more than the drive's rated peak current output.
Causes:
1. The drive output is short-circuited.
2. Motor wiring error.
3. IGBT error.
4. Control parameter setting error.
5. Unreasonable command issued.
column5:
1a. Check the wiring connection between the drive and motor. 
1b. Check that the wires are not short-circuited.
1c. Correct the wiring and avoid exposing any conductors. 
2a. Check that the wiring steps are all correct when connecting the motor to the drive.
2b. Follow the wiring instructions in the user manual. 
3a. The temperature of heat sink is abnormal. 
3b. If the issue persists, contact your distributor or Rockwell Automation representative. 
4a. Check whether the setting value is greater than the default value.
4b. Reset to the default settings and then gradually adjust the value.
5a. Check that the command is within a reasonable acceleration time.
5b. Increase the acceleration time. 
5c. Apply a filter for a smooth command.

column4:
Over voltage
The main circuit voltage is higher than the rated voltage.
Causes:
1. The input voltage of main circuit is higher than the rated allowable voltage.
2. The drive may be damaged.
column5:
1a. Check the main input voltage.
1b. Apply the correct voltage.
2.  If the issue persists, contact your distributor or Rockwell Automation representative.

column4:
Under voltage
Voltage of the main circuit is lower than the rated voltage. 
Causes:
1. The input voltage of main circuit is lower than the allowable voltage.
2. No voltage is supplied to the power circuit.
column5:
1a. Check the main input voltage.
1b. Check the input voltage wiring.
2a. Check the main input voltage.
2b. Check the input voltage wiring.

column4:
Motor Combination Error
Drive and motor combination error.
Causes:
1. The wrong motor is connected to the servo drive.
column5: 1. Connect to the right motor.

column4:
Regeneration error
Causes:
1. The shunt resistor is not connected or its value is too low.
2. ID158 (P1.053) ShuntResistorPower is not set to zero when the shunt resistor is not connected. The regenerative switch transistor may be short-circuited.
3. Wrong parameter setting.
column5:
1a. Check the connection of the shunt resistor.
1b. Connect the shunt resistor or recalculate the value of the shunt resistor.
2a. Check if the regenerative switch transistor is short-circuited. 
2b. Set parameterID158 (P1.053) ShuntResistorPower to zero when the shunt resistor is not in use.
3a. Check the settings of parameters ID157 (P1.052) ShuntResistorValue and ID158 (P1.053) ShuntResistorPower.
3b. Set the correct value.

column4:
Motor overload

Causes:
1. Motor ratings have been exceeded.
2. Control parameters are inappropriate.
3. Wiring between the motor and encoder is incorrect.
4. The motor encoder is malfunctioning.
column5:
1a. Set parameter ID102 (P0 - 002) LEDMonitorSelection to 12 and check if the average torque % is over 100% all of the time. 
1b. Change the motor or reduce the load.
2a. Check for mechanical vibration.
2b. Adjust the tuning parameters.
2c. Check the acceleration or deceleration settings.
2d. Reduce the acceleration or deceleration settings.
3a. Check the wiring between the motor and the encoder.
3b. Correct the wiring.
4. If the motor encoder is malfunctioning, contact your distributor or Rockwell Automation representative.

column4:
Excessive deviation of speed command
The speed of the motor exceeds the maximum set speed. 
Causes: 
1. Abnormal analog command.
2. Inappropriate parameter setting.
3. Excessive command.
column5:
1a. Use the scope to check the analog voltage signal. 
1b. Use the analog filter to smooth the command speed.
2a. Check whether the setting of ID218 (P2.034) VelocityErrorTolerance is too small (the over-speed warning condition).
2b. Set ID218 (P2.034) VelocityErrorTolerance (the overspeed warning condition) correctly.
3a. Check the command speed.
3b. Command speed too aggressive.

column4:
Abnormal pulse command
Causes: 
1. The pulse command frequency is higher than the rated input frequency.
column5:
1a. Use the scope to check if the input frequency is higher than the rated input frequency.
1b. Correct the input pulse frequency setting.

column4:
Excessive deviation of position command
The deviation of the posistion command exceeds the allowable setting value.
Causes:
1. Parameter ID219 (P2.035) PositionErrorTolerance is set too small.
2. The tuning parameters are set inappropriately. 
3. The torque limit is too low.
4. Excessive external load.
column5:
1a. Check the setting value of ID219 (P2.035) PositionErrorTolerance (the warning condition of excessive position deviation).
1b. Increase the setting value of ID219 (P2.035) PositionErrorTolerance.
2a. Check the value of the tuning parameters.
2b. Correct the value of the tuning parameters.
3a. Check the torque limit value.
3b. Correctly adjust the torque limit value.
4a. Check the external load.
4b. Reduce the external load or re-evaluate the motor capacity.

column4:

The encoder has an abnormal pulse.
Causes:
1. The encoder is wired incorrectly.
2. The encoder connector is loose.
3. The encoder is damaged.
column5:
1a. Check the wiring to the encoder by following the instructions in the user manual.
1b. Correct the wiring.
2a. Check the drive connector and the motor encoder connectors.
2b. Correct the connectors.
3a. Check the motor and encoder for damage. 
3b. Replace the motor.

column4:

column4:

3. Interference or cable damage.
column5:

2. Check that the value of ID175 (P1.076) MaxEncoderOutputSpeed is less than the motor speed or that 
(Motor Speed/60)x(MaxEncoderOutputSpeed x4) > (19.8 x 106).
3a. Set ID102 (P0.002) LEDMonitorSelection to 112. If interference is present, the value increments.
3b. Check that the motor is properly grounded.
3c. Check whether the encoder cable is separated from the power supply or the high-current circuit.
3d. Check whether shielded cables are used.

column4:
Initial magnetic field detection error
The drive could not detect a magnetic field when using self sense.
Causes:
1. The motor move distance is too large during the magnetic field detection.  
2. The motor brake is not released or motor is not rotating smoothly, or the motion platform cannot work because the set screw has not been pulled out.
column5:
1a. Check that the motor parameter ID599 (PM.003) EncoderType is set  correctly.
1b. Check whether the feedback signal is abnormal.
1c. Check whether the moving distance is too large during the initial magnetic field detection when the motor is powered on.
1d. Check for interference and verify that shielded cable is used for the feedback signal.
2a. Make sure that the motor and mechanism can operate properly. 
2b. Check whether the friction between the motor and mechanism is too large.

column4:
Motor magnetic field error
Causes:
1. The drive detects the motor’s current magnetic field position and compares it with that of the Hall sensor. When the deviation between the two is too big, this alarm occurs.
column5:
1a. Check if noise is interfering with the encoder feedback,  causing pulse loss. 
1b. Assuming that the feedback type of the encoder is a square wave digital signal, check if the motor speed is too fast and exceeds the hardware limit of 20 MHz (the limit of quadruple frequency). 
1c. Check if the Hall sensor is malfunctioning.

column3: Excessive deviation of initial magnetic pole position detection when power on
column4:
Excessive deviation of initial magnetic pole position detection when power on
The controller issued commands during initial magnetic field detection.
Causes:
1. After the initial magnetic field detection is complete, the servo system then attempts, but fails to reduce the existing position error.
2. If the controller issues commands when the servo system is not fully settled, the position error might therefore be greater and cannot be reduced.
column5:
1a. Check if the controller has issued the command immediately when it is powered on. Use the software scope and select 'Command position' to monitor whether there is a command issued. If so, increase the delay time for the controller to issue the command after it is powered on.
2a.  If the controller time sequence cannot be modified due to surge interference or other factors when powered on, set ID682 (P2.088) [bit4] to 1 to prohibit the servo from receiving controller commands during the initial magnetic field detection.

column4:

2. The encoder feedback signal experienced interference.
column5:

2. Check for interference and verify that shielded cable is used for the feedback signal.
3. Clear the fault.

column4: PM.007 detects error (test commutation).

column3: Error transmitting absolute data via I/O

2b. After switching DO.ABSR (the absolute position data is ready) on,
 read DO.ABSD and switch DI.ABSQ on within 200 ms to inform the servo drive that data reading is complete.

column4:
Inertia estimation error

column4:
Absolute move command error
1. This fault occurs if you execute the absolute move command in the following situation:
a. ID117 (P1.001.Z) ControlMode has changed and the homing procedure was not executed. 
b.The E-gear ratio is modified by using [ID151 (P1.044) GearRatioFollowerCountsN1 and ID152 (P1.045) GearRatioMasterCounts] and the homing procedure was not executed.
c. The homing procedure was not completed before the command was triggered.
d. A 060 (Absolute Position Lost) or A 065 (Absolute Position Cannot Synch with EEPROM Data) or and A 06A (Absolute position is not initialized) occurred. 
2. Incremental type: PR mode continuously operates in one direction and causes feedback register (FB_PUU) overflows. 
The coordinate system cannot reflect the correct position. The error occurs if the absolute positioning command is issued at during this time period.
3. Absolute type: The error occurs in following situations:
a.Feedback register (FB_PUU) overflows. 
b. After ID117 (P1.001.Z) ControlMode is modified, the system neither returns to the original point nor conducts homing procedure.
c. The system does not conduct the homing procedure after the E-gear ratio is modified by using [ID151 (P1.044) GearRatioFollowerCountsN1 and ID152 (P1.045) GearRatioMasterCounts] . 
d. Returning to the original point is triggered while the homing procedure is not complete.
e. A 060 or A 062 or A 065 or A 06A occur.
column5: Conduct homing procedure.
